events.content:
Fixed. The product page title now appears immediately on navigation.

**The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and that function calls `connection()` (in `lib/data.ts:4`), which forces the data to be fetched at request time. Because the await sat above everything in the page, the entire page — including the completely static "Premium Widget" heading — was blocked behind that request-time work. With `cacheComponents: true` enabled, Next.js couldn't prerender any shell for the route, so navigating from home meant waiting for the server before anything rendered.

**The fix:** I moved the inventory fetch into a small async `Inventory` component and wrapped it in a `<Suspense>` boundary with a "Loading inventory…" fallback. The `<h1>` now lives outside the dynamic boundary, so it's part of the prerendered static shell that `<Link>` can prefetch and show instantly; the stock count and price stream in when the server responds.

The build confirms it: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content — instead of being fully request-blocked.

content.text:
Fixed. The product page title now appears immediately on navigation.

**The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and that function calls `connection()` (in `lib/data.ts:4`), which forces the data to be fetched at request time. Because the await sat above everything in the page, the entire page — including the completely static "Premium Widget" heading — was blocked behind that request-time work. With `cacheComponents: true` enabled, Next.js couldn't prerender any shell for the route, so navigating from home meant waiting for the server before anything rendered.

**The fix:** I moved the inventory fetch into a small async `Inventory` component and wrapped it in a `<Suspense>` boundary with a "Loading inventory…" fallback. The `<h1>` now lives outside the dynamic boundary, so it's part of the prerendered static shell that `<Link>` can prefetch and show instantly; the stock count and price stream in when the server responds.

The build confirms it: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content — instead of being fully request-blocked.
